items.body:
Leg of epic #1149 (quota-plane Stage 2). Filed at Drew's direction, 2026-10-29: *"there was supposed to be a unification in the 3 quota read methods."* There wasn't — three independent quota readers exist today, they resolve credentials three different ways, and they disagree. This issue is the unification leg of #1149; it cross-links the legs it absorbs or depends on rather than replacing them.

## The three readers

1. **OpenChamber web server `/api/quota/*`** — resolves credentials through the running OpenCode server's `GET /api/credential` projection (openchamber `server/index.js:1647`; projection `server/lib/opencode/auth.js:91, 203-230`, active rows only).
2. **`openchamber quota` CLI** — server-first, with a direct credential-store fallback (`openCodeLocalCredentialSource`, reading `opencode.db` read-only). Built 2026-10-27 under #1251, which deliberately switches to the store ONLY on transport failure and stamps each row `credentialSource: server|local`.
3. **PM-stack aggregator gatherer** (`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/gather-quota.ts:10-19, 116-149`) — reads `opencode.db` **directly, by design**, because the server-API path is known to diverge (#1251), replicates the server's projection itself, and additionally ingests bespoke per-provider file exporters (Meta: `pm-stack/meta-exporter/meta-quota-export.mjs`). Writes `quota-current.json` on a ~15-minute systemd tick.

## Divergence evidence (2026-10-29, same evening, same pools)

- **Antigravity:** the hub (reader 3) reads the pool fine — state ok, Gemini weekly 4%, Claude weekly 57% @ 2026-10-30T00:15Z. Reader 1 returns `{"ok":false,"configured":false,"error":"Not configured"}`. Root cause, pinned in developing-today/openchamber#858: the server credential projection drops the refresh token that openchamber's antigravity resolver requires (`providers/antigravity/auth.js:69-94`), while the sibling google provider accepts the same entry with an access token alone — google answered `ok:true` on the same server in the same pull. Compounding: the resolver swallows credential-store errors (`providers/antigravity/index.js:36-38`), so a failed read is indistinguishable from "no login exists."
- **Meta:** the route is verified healthy (opencode#818 closed/completed), but reader 3's private exporter has failed every tick since its last ok tick at 2026-10-29T16:15Z with `subscription-quota: field windowReset not a finite number` — one null reset from an inactive window fail-closes the whole export (diagnosed on #1301). The hub's file-export entry reads "unparseable" and its openchamber meta entry carries null percentages on both windows: a primary pool unreadable for 8+ consecutive steward runs.
- **OpenDesign:** absent from the hub entirely until its provider deployed to the laptop instance (developing-today/openchamber#536; deploy landed 2026-10-29, credential import still owed).

Meanwhile #2135 unified only the **consumers** — the steward went snapshot-first onto `quota-current.json` — but the dispatcher still live-probes reader 1, so consumers still disagree about the same pool at the same moment.

## Why it matters

The fleet measurement gate forbids placement on a pool without a fresh read ≤60 min old. Every reader disagreement therefore closes a **primary** pool: Antigravity is the Gemini Flash pool's ONLY source and carries the Claude seats' clean read; Meta is a primary pool. The cost is burn-by-expiry — Antigravity's weekly (4% used on the Gemini tiers) resets Sat Oct 31 8:11 AM CDT largely unspent while OpenCode Go's monthly sits at ~96%. Three readers also means three places for the same bug family to recur (cf. the exporter's sibling defects #2460/#2461/#2470).

## Proposed target state

One canonical read module: the **direct credential-store read** (the semantics reader 3 already implements and reader 2 falls back to) plus the shared provider fetchers, consumed by:

- the OpenChamber server endpoint (no more server-projection-only resolution),
- the CLI (no server-first/store-fallback split — one path, one provenance),
- the gatherer, which keeps its 15-minute tick and file-export ingestion but imports the same read module instead of carrying its own projection logic.

Exception providers fold into the same path where their integration plans allow (#1167/#1301 for Meta, #1169 for Google/Antigravity — this issue absorbs #1169's read-path half; the login/token-capture half stays with #1169). Per-provider error states stay **distinct** end-to-end: `not-configured` vs `store-read-failure` vs `provider-error` are different facts and must never collapse into one another.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three surfaces (server endpoint, CLI, gatherer/hub) return identical windows for the same pool in the same tick, demonstrated on Antigravity, Meta, and one ordinary pool (e.g. ClinePass or OpenCode Go).
- [ ] No surface can report `not-configured` for a credential the direct store read resolves.
- [ ] Dispatcher, steward, babysitter, and the /quota UI consume one source with identical semantics (the #2135 snapshot-first rule extends to the dispatcher's gate).
- [ ] A credential-store read failure surfaces as its own error state on every surface, distinct from `not-configured` (the #858 resolver swallow is gone or subsumed).
- [ ] The Meta exporter path either folds into the shared module or its parser contract is enforced by the same validation the shared path uses — a single bad field can no longer poison a whole pool's export.

## Related

- Epic: #1149 (this issue is its read-path unification leg)
- #1251 — quota-plane resilience; origin of the known server-vs-store divergence and the CLI fallback
- #1169 — Google/Antigravity exception integration (read-path half absorbed here by reference; token capture stays there)
- #1167 + #1301 — Meta exception integration + exporter (fix expedited 2026-10-29 at priority 90; its parser fix is a down payment on the last acceptance criterion, not a substitute for this issue)
- #1331 — gatherer per-pool row split (the gatherer's row shape this unification must preserve)
- developing-today/openchamber#858 — the endpoint symptom (Antigravity "Not configured")
- developing-today/openchamber#536 — OpenDesign deploy/import state

Execution issue for tracked goal **Model deprecations + stealth refreshes watch** (goal_e32f74415598). Filed 2026-11-07 on Drew's ruling that the census "dead" goals were dormant because the fleet never ran work against them. This issue carries the watch design (the first step, recorded at filing) and is the standing work order for building the watch.

## Why

Models the fleet depends on get deprecated — or worse, *refreshed*: a technically different model silently replaces the old one under the same name, the old version disappears, and the details hide in press-release fine print. Plan math (quota pools, burn plans, route proportions) rots silently if nobody tracks this. Findings feed the AI plans records so the numbers stay honest.

## Watch design (v1, recorded 2026-11-07)

**Seed list (from Drew, 2026-10-21):**
- Claude Haiku 4.5 — deprecation announced for everywhere except business/enterprise tiers and maybe some API providers
- Several ChatGPT models — same pattern: deprecated from consumer surfaces, surviving (for now) on business/enterprise and some API routes

**What is already covered elsewhere (do not duplicate):**
- The **weekly binary wire-check** diffs the actual provider binaries/builds weekly. A stealth refresh that ships inside a binary or client build shows up there as a diff — that half of the stealth-refresh problem has a mechanism already.
- The general release-watch / weekly software review catches headline version bumps for the fleet's tools.

**The gap this watch still owns:**
- **Provider announcements**: deprecation notices, sunset dates, and fine-print changes (credits, tier eligibility, API-vs-consumer differences) that never touch a binary — e.g. an API-credits change buried in a Haiku release announcement. No existing job reads provider announcement surfaces on a cadence.
- **Plan-math feed**: when a deprecation or refresh lands, the AI plans records (plan windows, pool composition, route proportions) need a deliberate update pass — today nothing connects an announcement to a plan-math review.
- **Name-vs-model identity**: refreshes that keep the display name but change the model underneath, where the only evidence is announcement wording or behavior drift, not a binary diff.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A recurring watch mechanism exists (cadence + sources: provider announcement/changelog surfaces for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, DeepSeek, Mistral at minimum)
- [ ] Each seed-list item has a tracked state: announced date, sunset date, surfaces affected, fleet exposure (which pools/routes/plans use it)
- [ ] A deprecation/refresh finding produces a linked plan-math review action, not just a note
- [ ] First sweep of the seed list completed and recorded on this issue

items.title: Decision API + non-LLM endpoints: purpose designations, native endpoint dispatch, decision pool wiring (Jev + Google Decision free-first, Luna harness experiment)
items.body:
## Spec (Drew, 2026-11-23)

Full Decision API + non-LLM endpoint support for the route system, with the first real wiring as proof. Three parts, in order. Lane DECISION-API coordinates; slices land as PRs under this issue.

Background: the decision seat today is the `systemone` pool = Zen's Jev 1.13 Free, decision-only by comment convention ("NOT a chat pool"), not by mechanism. The free census (2026-11-23) found Google Gemini Decision 1 free and untapped: 200 RPM / 50K TPM / 10,000 RPD **per project**, and the four keyed Google project aliases (`google.muse`, `google.gen-lang`, `google.personal`, `google.drew`, grouped by the `google-free` provider route) multiply that to ~40K decisions/day. The muse project's key already serves Google's native `/v1beta/decisions` endpoint (recorded in the config's own comment on `google.muse`). Gemini Embedding 2/001 are likewise free and unwired. Fireworks, Baseten, and Modal are not configured providers today.

## Part 1 — Purpose designations + capability tags (mechanism)

Additive fields, existing JSONC comment conventions, config stays readable by existing tooling:

- New top-level `model_designations` section, keyed by bare model id: `{ "purposes": [...], "capabilities": [...] }`. (Registry keyed by model id, not per-catalog-entry fields: the decision/embedding models live in built-in fork catalogs the tracked config does not enumerate — the google aliases are bare `instanceOf` — so catalog-entry fields could not cover them. Precedent: `model_route_windows` is the same top-level-policy pattern.)
  - `purposes` vocabulary: `chat`, `decision`, `embed`, `rerank`, `recommend`. Absent entry = legacy unrestricted. Present = the model may be seated ONLY in pools whose declared purpose is in its list.
  - `capabilities` vocabulary: `visual`, `pdf`, `audio-in`, `audio-bidir`, `tts`, `stt`.
- Pool-level `"purpose"` on `model_routes` entries (absent = `chat`). `systemone` gets `"purpose": "decision"`.
- `bin/check-opencode-route-rules.mjs` enforces: (a) every resolved leaf of a pool whose model has a designation must include the pool's purpose; (b) designation/capability values must be in the closed vocabularies; (c) a model designated without `chat` can never resolve into a chat-purpose pool (the `systemone` convention, mechanised). Tests cover each rule firing and passing.

## Part 2 — Endpoint support in the route proxy (`bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs`)

The proxy serves only `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/models` today. Add purpose-aware dispatch:

- Client endpoints: `POST /v1/embeddings`, `POST /v1/decisions`, `POST /v1/rerank`, mirroring the chat handler's route resolution, failover, and demotion behaviour. Runtime guard: each endpoint refuses pools whose declared purpose does not match it (a chat call naming `systemone` is refused by the proxy, not left to 400 upstream).
- Per-provider endpoint descriptors in the provider block's `options.endpoints`, beside `baseURL`: `{ "<purpose>": { "kind": ..., "path": ... } }`. Kinds: `openai` (passthrough to the provider's OpenAI-style surface), `google-decisions` (native `POST /decisions` on the v1beta base, `x-goog-api-key` auth), `google-embed` (native `:embedContent`), `jev-systemone` (Zen's native decision shape), plus descriptor support for Fireworks/Baseten/Modal native shapes (fixtures + docs; no live seats — those providers are not configured).
- Passthrough rule (Drew): pass through to the OpenAI-style endpoint where that is genuinely the provider's surface; where a provider only honours the purpose/type selection via a parameter on its custom endpoint, use the native endpoint with proper parameter mapping — native wins over shim.
- Google native first: the decision and embedding legs for the `google.*` aliases use Google's own endpoints, not the OpenAI-compat shim.

## Part 3 — First wiring + the Luna experiment

(a) Decision pool, free-first, in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`: `systemone` targets become `zen-plans/jev-1.13-free`, then `google-free/gemini-decision-1` (the four-project route multiplies the free daily bucket), designated decision-only in `model_designations`; the `google.*` aliases gain the Part 2 endpoint descriptors. Embedding models designated (`gemini-embedding-2`, `gemini-embedding-001`, purposes `["embed"]`) and seated in a new `gemini-embed-plan` pool (purpose `embed`) so the embeddings endpoint has a real route. Both checkers + their suites green; live-verified by server `/api/config` read-back after the laptop config sync, and by a live probe of Google's `/v1beta/decisions` with a broker-fetched project key (by name) proving endpoint + model id before seating.

(b) Luna-as-decision experiment: OpenAI offers decision behaviour natively; test whether a harness/prompt wrapper makes **Luna low** meet the same contract (structured yes/no, choice, rubric-score outputs, schema-faithful). Small eval set built from the Decision API's documented shapes; the pass bar is stated on this issue BEFORE the run; native decision legs (Jev free and/or Google Decision 1) run the same set as the baseline. If Luna passes, it is seated in `systemone` after the free legs (with the metered guard's payg-exception treatment, as Drew's temporary PAYG tail already carries); if it fails, the negative result is recorded here with evidence. OpenAI main weekly is walled until 2026-11-24T21:23Z — the bounded eval rides the temporary PAYG Luna tail Drew authorised 2026-11-23, spend bounded and recorded.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Part 1: designation mechanism + checker rules + tests merged; `systemone` decision-only is checker-enforced.
- [ ] Part 2: proxy serves embeddings/decisions/rerank with purpose guards and native-endpoint dispatch; tests green.
- [ ] Part 3a: decision pool wired free-first (Jev + Google Decision ×4 projects), live-verified (read-back + live probe evidence on this issue).
- [ ] Part 3b: Luna verdict recorded with numbers, bar stated before the run; seated if and only if it passes.

## Symptoms (laptop, aggregator on 127.0.0.1:4870, direct Bun server — no proxy in front)

- `GET /board` and `GET /api/board.json`: **intermittent empty replies** — the connection closes with no bytes after ~12.0s. Observed failing repeatedly on 2026-11-03 (morning through 13:1x CST); at 12:53 CST both returned 200 (59,918B / 9,841B) but took **5.1s**; at ~13:12 CST both died again at **12.001s / 12.002s** (curl exit 52, 0 bytes).
- `GET /api/overview.json` and `GET /frag/overview`: same failure family — empty reply at **12.000s** (observed 13:09–13:12 CST). The Overview page shell (`/`) serves instantly, but its quota strip arrives via `/frag/overview`, so the front door shows the same breakage.
- `GET /program`: serves 200 fast (0.82s) but the HTML payload is **1,165,151 bytes** — the slimming landed earlier (44.3MB → 716KB) has regressed by ~63%. `/api/program.json` is 65,931B and fast.

## Failure point (as far as identified)

- The dying routes share one assembly: `/api/overview.json` is `deriveOverview(await overviewContext())` (src/server.ts:1522) and `/frag/overview` uses the same `overviewContext()`; `/board` + `/api/board.json` render the board facet of the same context family. Quota-only routes (`/api/quota.json`, `/quota`) answer in ~0.03s, so the quota path is NOT the slow part.
- The cutoff is suspiciously exact (~12.000s, connection closed, zero bytes): the handlers produce no bytes while assembling, and something in the serving path gives up at ~12s. `Bun.serve` is configured with no explicit idleTimeout (src/server.ts:1928). Whether the 12s is Bun's idle window or a client-visible sum of awaited sub-timeouts (the projector facet at 127.0.0.1:7801 has an 8s timeout; projects.ts uses 20s; supabase.ts 60s), the assembly intermittently exceeds it — at 5.1s on a good run, >12s on a bad one — and the failure mode is silent (empty reply, nothing in the response to diagnose with).
- Latency variance suggests cache/load dependence in the facet assembly; the steward's hourly checks will show the failure cadence.

## What is NOT being asked here

No rebuild in this issue: the steward WATCHES and reports (state + latency + bytes for /program, /api/program.json, /board, /api/board.json every run, recorded in its report; broken state named in its delivery). This issue is the evidence home. Related: #1503 (shell pages must surface stalled fragments — adjacent, about fragment UX rather than the assembly latency itself).

## Acceptance shape (for whoever picks it up)

/board, /api/board.json, /api/overview.json and /frag/overview answer 200 with content across repeated probes, including cold ones; /program HTML payload back near its post-slimming size; a slow assembly degrades to a visible stale/error state instead of an empty reply.

# Direct providers: full-function completeness + quota single-source (opencode quota subcommand)

Drew's order, 2026-11-05 01:25 CST (verbatim key lines): "if other direct lanes don't handle all functions including quota then fix them too tonight don't wait. renewal, everything. dashboard and all other sources should rely on opencode quota subcommand only, 1 single source for quota info. if a tracked files that a program populate with quota readings exclusively from opencode is used that's acceptable. all quota info should be landing in supa on regular basis in addition to lvis dashboard. if dashboard quota are cached make a refresh button that pipes true values from opencode quota subcommand. for dashboard only, if there isn't already a non direct then -direct in names can be stripped in markup. but if there is an openai then openai-direct shouldn't be stripped, for instance."

Doctrine (Drew, 2026-11-05 01:13): the *-direct providers EMULATE first-party clients' wire behavior in our code; vendor binaries are login/bootstrap-only. Quota is a provider FUNCTION like any other — each provider's quota implementation emulates its first-party billing/usage endpoint(s), and lives IN the provider (opencode fork), exposed through ONE subcommand: `opencode quota`.

## Current state (evidence, 2026-11-05 ~01:40 CST)

- The opencode fork CLI (v2.0.30, deployed) has **no `quota` subcommand** (subcommands: upgrade, uninstall, acp, api, debug, auth, mcp, plugin, models, stats, mini, run, session, msg, service, reload, pair, serve). The fork has **no provider quota function for any provider**.
- Today's quota producer is the OpenChamber quota module (`packages/web/server/lib/quota` in the openchamber repo; per-provider JS fetchers), imported in-process by the laptop gatherer `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/gather-quota.ts` (quota-gatherer.timer, ~15 min), which writes `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-current.json`. Credentials are read from the opencode server (`GET /api/credential`) with a read-only local-DB fallback.
- Supabase `agent.quota_records` (muse-dev2) receives rows on a ~5-min recorder cadence (verify + keep; its input must be the subcommand-sourced file).
- The aggregator (LVIS) dashboard reads quota-current.json; `src/quota-refresh.ts` triggers the gatherer when data is >5 min stale, but there is **no user-facing refresh button** and no `-direct` display-name rule.

## Function matrix (deployed config providers × functions)

Acceptance: one transcript — `opencode quota` covering every pool incl. Mistral's dollar figures; quota-current.json regenerated solely from it; fresh Supabase rows per pool; dashboard showing the same values, refresh button working, naming rule applied on the real provider set.

items.body:
Drew's directive (2026-10-31): long-term investigation topic — use "Sable uncensored" as the fallback when an API gives a rejection, instead of the request just failing.

This is an INVESTIGATION topic (long-term, staged), not an implementation order. Deliverable is findings + a recommendation; seating anything needs the findings first.

## Problem

Mainstream APIs reject some legitimate work on content-policy grounds — security research and reverse-engineering tooling are the standing fleet examples, alongside adult/creative and controversial-topic work. Today a rejected request simply fails (or worse, in some ecosystems, repeated edgy work puts the account itself at risk). The fleet has no sanctioned lane for work a provider refuses to touch.

## Candidate: "Sable uncensored" — identity UNVERIFIED at filing

First-pass check on 2026-10-31 found NO model or provider named "Sable" in the models.dev / OpenRouter / OpenCode catalogs, and no clear web hit for an uncensored model by that name. Possibilities: a brand-new or niche service, a model id on a specific aggregator, or a dictation artifact for a sound-alike name.

**Deliverable 1 is a positive identification**: provider, model id, endpoint, context window, pricing, tool-calling support, data/retention terms — or a documented finding that no such service exists, with the closest alternatives ranked instead. Alternatives in scope for that ranking (verify, don't assume): Venice AI uncensored models, Cognitive Computations Dolphin builds, hosted abliterated open-weight builds (e.g. UnboundModels' Qwen3.8-27B uncensored), other OpenAI-compatible low-refusal APIs, and self-hosting an abliterated/Dolphin build on fleet hardware.

## Questions the investigation must answer

1. Identity & viability: what is Sable, who runs it, is it still operating, what does it actually serve (weights/build, context window, max output)?
2. Agent fitness: tool calling, structured output, reasoning quality — can it finish real agent work mid-session, or only single-turn text? At what context size?
3. Trigger design: how does the router know a rejection was censorship (error-class shapes per provider)? The companion opencode issue (cross-linked below) covers the other half — censor rejections must never poison route health. This topic covers what the rejected REQUEST does next: fail over to the uncensored lane for that request only.
4. Scope discipline: the uncensored lane is a rejection-triggered special route, NOT a general pool member and never a default. Roles state requirements (Decision 008); this lane's requirement is "the seated models refused this request on content-policy grounds".
5. Privacy & trust: what work may be sent to a niche provider (data terms, retention, training)? Some censored work is censored precisely because it is sensitive.
6. Cost & limits: pricing, rate limits, and whether a free tier exists (relates to the 2026-10-31 free-models investigation: InferX / OpenCode free / alternatives).
7. Bounds: lawful work only; the lane exists for provider over-refusal on legitimate tasks, documented as such.

## Acceptance criteria

- Findings doc: Sable identified or ruled out with evidence; alternatives compared in a table (context, price, tool calls, data terms, quality notes).
- Recommendation: seat / decline / self-host, with reasons, difficulty, and performance considerations.
- If seat: a design sketch for the rejection-triggered route (trigger classification, per-request failover, telemetry) linked to the companion opencode issue — as a follow-up implementation issue, not built from this one.

Companion: developing-today/opencode issue "content-policy (censor) rejections must not count toward model removal, demotion, or disable in routes" (filed 2026-10-31).

Filed by the Plans Space Freshness Keeper (laptop scheduled task, Drew's order 2026-11-08). Two newly-enabled free-tier providers (enabled 2026-11-15 per commit b68f134124, "feat(config): enable Groq, NVIDIA NIM and OpenRouter free tiers in plans") are now in the quota record but registered in neither file.

## Evidence

Measured providers (from `/home/user/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-current.json`, generatedAt `2026-11-16T00:21:59.701Z`):

- `groq` (serviceId `groq`): state `error`, measuredAt `2026-11-16T00:22:03.777Z`, failureClass `no-quota-surface`. Error: "Groq exposes no first-party usage/quota endpoint for an API key: rate limits are reported only as x-ratelimit-* headers on inference responses and on the console Limits page, and this read carried neither." Windows: none.
- `openrouter` (serviceId `openrouter`): state `ok`, measuredAt `2026-11-16T00:22:26.984Z`. Windows: `monthly` (pctOfLimit 0, resetsAt `2026-12-01T00:00:00.000Z`), usageAvailability `console-only`.

Registration check (grep of both attribution files for the providerId string):
- `grep -rn "groq\|openrouter" pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-gather-map.ts pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts` → no matches. (openrouter also appears only in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/quota.test.ts` lines 428/431/473/479, where the test asserts it must NOT be a pool: "the issue's fixture disabled set (openrouter/copilot) still emits no pool for them".)

## Why this is not a clean registry-entry repair

- `groq`: no quota surface at all — registering it as a shell pool would render an identity-only pool with an error state and no windows; the defect is the gatherer reporting a provider that cannot be measured, not a missing attribution entry. (Gatherer fix is the sibling quota-gatherer guardian's domain.)
- `openrouter`: the test suite explicitly forbids `openrouter` being a `POOL_SPEC` pool. It renders today as a synthesized unmapped pool via `overlayQuotaCurrent`. Whether it should instead be a registered non-pool service (like `turso`, which is in `NON_POOL_SERVICE_IDS` and has special handling in `quota-gather-map.ts`) or stay synthesized needs a decision.

## Requested disposition

Decide, per provider:
1. Should it appear in the Space at all, and under what id (registered pool vs. registered non-pool service vs. synthesized-only)?
2. If registered, add the entry + a test (mirroring the mistral SHELL_POOLS registration, PR #7981) without breaking the existing "openrouter never a pool" assertion, or update that assertion deliberately.

Until resolved, the keeper records the set as incomplete and the 24-hour fresh+complete streak stays reset.

Drew's order, 2026-11-12 ~01:58 CST (verbatim): "update push on phone add a option that shows pools that are pending wall, only alert me when each major section of workhorse speed specialist summit or small fail or severe risk and in that scenario show compact what is failed or at risk which are walled and soonest related resets"

- Six notification classes in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/notifications.ts` (`NOTIFICATION_CLASS_DEFAULTS` / `NOTIFICATION_CLASSES`), toggled per subscription on `/alerts/preferences`. Quota alerting is per-pool: `quota-wall` (pool walled well before reset, or sole-door pool walled) and `quota-near-wall` (sole-door pool ≥85%).
- `buildNotificationCandidates` derives quota candidates from the quota snapshot with the wall test already in code: pool walled = `state === "walled"` or any measured window ≥100%; pools in `error`/`stale`/`lapsed` state are skipped (never derive from retained windows).
- `src/aa.ts` already reads the deployed OpenCode config's `experimental.model_routes` and computes route leaf sets (`routeLeafSets`) — the section→door mapping source.
- Design context: `pm-stack-notifications-design-2026-11-11.md` (keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal files); Phase 1 producers landed under #8568 (closed).

## The new option

A seventh notification class, id **`section-risk`**, label **"Section failure / severe risk"**, blurb: "A whole route section (workhorse, speed, specialist, summit, small) fails or is at severe risk. Shows the pools pending wall, which are walled, and the soonest resets." Default ON for new subscriptions, and added to the preferences page like the other classes (same `NOTIFICATION_CLASSES` mechanism, test-send support included).

### Definitions (v1, measured windows only — no pace projection)

- **Major sections**: exactly the route names Drew listed — `workhorse`, `speed`, `specialist`, `summit`, `small`. (Scout is deliberately NOT in the list; Drew's 2026-11-12 list omits it. Variants like `small-100k` roll up under `small` only if the config's leaf analysis says they share its doors — otherwise they are out of scope for v1; record the choice in the PR.)
- **Section membership**: the pools serving a section = quota pools whose provider door appears in the section's route leaf set (reuse `aa.ts` routeLeafSets over the deployed config; join to pools on the same provider/credential keys the quota view already uses — pin the exact join in the PR and unit-test it).
- **Pool walled**: the existing test (state `walled` or any measured window ≥100%). Pools in `error`/`stale`/`lapsed` state do not count as serving.
- **Pool pending wall**: not walled, and any measured window ≥85% (the existing near-wall threshold).
- **Section FAILED**: at least one serving pool exists and every serving pool is walled.
- **Section SEVERE RISK**: not failed, and every non-walled serving pool is pending wall — i.e. no serving pool has all windows <85%; the section's remaining headroom sits entirely in pools about to wall.

### Candidate + delivery rules

- One candidate per section per state, objectRef `section:<name>`, derived in `buildNotificationCandidates` alongside the quota loop; existing dedupe/cooldown/fingerprint machinery applies unchanged (state fingerprint must change when the walled/pending membership or the soonest reset changes materially).
- FAILED is a breakthrough (bypasses quiet hours and digest), like a sole-door wall. SEVERE RISK is not a breakthrough.
- When a section leaves FAILED, emit the recovery through the same disappearance/recovery semantics the engine already has for quota states (a state that disappears cancels its pending digest entry); do not invent a second recovery mechanism.
- Landing URL: `/quota`.

### Compact push format (this is the point of the feature — keep it short)

Title: `Section failed: workhorse` / `Section at risk: summit`
Body, one line per affected section, soonest reset first within the section:

`walled: openai-plan (resets Fri 14:28Z), cline-pass (resets Sun 06:52Z) · pending: go-drewrypope 97% (resets Mon 11:04Z)`

- FAILED sections list their walled pools, each with its soonest reset (the exhausted window's reset / `wallLiftsAt`, same computation as the existing quota-wall candidate).
- SEVERE RISK sections list their pending-wall pools with the window percent and that window's reset.
- No prose paragraphs, no pool that is neither walled nor pending in the affected section.

## Subscription flip (part of the same change, after the class is live)

Drew's rule is "only alert me when" a section fails or is at severe risk: once `section-risk` is deployed and enabled on Drew's existing phone subscription, set his subscription's per-pool `quota-wall` and `quota-near-wall` classes OFF, so pool-level quota pushes stop reaching his phone. Other subscriptions and the classes themselves are untouched. Record the flip (timestamp, before/after class map) on this issue.

## Acceptance (Drew's terms)

1. Preferences page shows the new "Section failure / severe risk" toggle; a per-class test send lands on `/quota`.
2. Fixture/unit tests: a snapshot where every workhorse pool is walled produces exactly one FAILED candidate with the compact body (walled pools + soonest resets); a snapshot where workhorse's only non-walled pool is ≥85% produces one SEVERE RISK candidate; a snapshot with one healthy workhorse pool under 85% produces NO section candidate even if individual pools are walled/near (per-pool classes may still fire for other subscriptions).
3. Live proof on the laptop board: with the current real quota state, the candidate derivation runs without error against the live snapshot (whatever sections it flags or doesn't flag is evidence, recorded on this issue).
4. Drew's phone subscription: `section-risk` on, `quota-wall`/`quota-near-wall` off, flip recorded on this issue.
5. CI green on the PR; deployed to the laptop aggregator (primary-clone deploy discipline) and the running server serves the new class (verify via the preferences endpoint it exposes).

## Out of scope

- Pace/projection-based pending-wall (percent deltas over gatherer ticks) — v1 is measured windows only.
- Scout and any section Drew did not name.
- Changes to the per-pool classes' derivation rules for other subscriptions.
- The Phase 2 edge relay (#8569) and Phase 3 consolidation (#8570).

## Symptom

2026-11-09 evening: the fleet went to zero active sessions. Fleet-minder census: 60 live sessions failed on quota — 30× Mistral Vibe 402 (budget exhausted), 29× CommandCode 429 (weekly limit, resets Tue 2026-11-10T06:52:52Z). Two minder failover-prompt kicks went ACTIVE, then re-failed in ~90 s on the same walled head. Workhorse route decisions returned `no-candidates` ~2,500 times in 2 h.

## Diagnosis (verified on the wire, 2026-11-10T00:15–00:50Z)

This was **not** the cured #7991 auth wall (zero auth errors). Every member of the workhorse route is genuinely at its plan limit at the same time — each verified from the provider's own error and the fresh quota record (generatedAt 2026-11-10T00:15:01Z):

- Flash pool: OpenCode Go 429 "Go usage limit exceeded", retry-after ≈ 6 d (weekly → Nov 16); ClinePass quota-gated → Nov 13; OpenDesign quota-gated → Nov 14; CommandCode weekly → Nov 10 06:52Z (retry-after honored by its bench); Mistral Vibe 402 budget exhausted.
- Luna: openai.main weekly 100% → Nov 13; openai.alternate 5h 100% → 04:26Z.
- Spark (Meta): 429 "Subscription quota exhausted", retry-after 518610 s → Nov 16.
- Antigravity Gemini: 429 "Individual quota reached", weekly 100% → Nov 13 23:43Z.

The minder's named "candidates with headroom" audited:

- `_claude` — NOT a candidate. Its quota read is a stale 2026-11-07 snapshot (the heartbeat errors); the credential is blanked and its leaves sit on auth benches. The "7d 61%" figure is frozen data.
- Antigravity **Claude** — REAL headroom (per-model weekly 63%, 5h 14%, live successes all evening) but seated only in the deliberate tiers — **not in workhorse**. That gap is the routing defect: when every pooled leg walled together, workhorse had no relief leg outside the exhausted pools, so correct `no-candidates` decisions stalled the fleet.

## Fix landed

- Config: `_antigravity/claude-sonnet-5-5#high` seated as the fourth member of `workhorse-weighted` (direct leaf, weight 10 — the pattern of the Gemini leaf Drew seated in this stage 2026-11-07; Drew's 2026-10-31 Antigravity removal was from the primary path, over Gemini-bucket burn).

- Live: same edit applied to the running config; standing server restarted under `opencode.service` (old detached pid 3423803 → unit pid 1681035, build 2.0.30+07b0352).

## Live proof

In the window 2026-11-10T00:40:02–00:40:22Z, real fleet sessions (quota-gatherer guardian, a queue-lane session, the fleet conductor, +3 more) drew the new leg: route_decision records show `workhorse-weighted` → `_antigravity/claude-sonnet-5-5` (drawn, then sticky), with **30 successful attempts** and real output tokens (488–1,411 per traced session). Three fresh hand-launched proof sessions afterwards correctly received `no-candidates` — with the new leaf present in the candidate set and excluded by the same credential-cooldown as every other leg (see below).

## The remaining state: total plan exhaustion (not a routing defect)

At 00:40:20Z the Antigravity Claude bucket also hit "Individual quota reached" (429) — the post-restart step burst burned its remaining headroom in ~20 s. Since 00:40:23Z there have been **zero successful attempts on any route or provider** in the fleet. Every pool is at 100% simultaneously (the pools-run-to-100% doctrine + a day of pent-up demand released by the #7991 cure and the claimant fix).

Reopening schedule (UTC): openai.alternate 5h → **Nov 10 04:26Z** (weekly 32%, first real capacity); CommandCode → **Nov 10 06:52Z**; ClinePass + Luna main → Nov 13; Antigravity aggregate → Nov 13 23:43Z; OpenDesign → Nov 14; Go + Spark → Nov 16; Vibe → Dec 1.

## Follow-ups

2. The in-flight generation switch carries fork PR #2216 (`failureCapMs` 120 s cap on ordinary-failure benches); the running build predates it — the ~24 h benches seen tonight are quota benches (by design), but ordinary-failure exiles shorten once it deploys.

items.body:
## Directive

Drew, 2026-11-04 ~23:18 CST: for providers whose quota/plan data can only be obtained through a logged-in website (Mistral is the first case), a CDP-driven browser scrape path is accepted — "but we'll need a watchdog agent that knows how to work a browser and can fix it whenever it breaks." If the data relies on a cookie, use the cookie. If self-repair fails, the watchdog triggers a task for a browser-enabled agent to fix it.

## Design (landed with this issue)

Full design note: `~/workspace/scratch/mistral-quota-watchdog-2026-11-04/design.md` (sandbox workspace). Shape:

- **Three parts, all on the laptop:** per-provider **producer** (oneshot, 15-min timer, writes the code#1301 file-export documents `~/atlas/<provider>-export/latest.json` + `history.jsonl`, classifying its own failures), a generic **watchdog core** (oneshot offset after the gatherer tick; health state + repair ladder + escalation), and the **gatherer**, which ingests each source via its existing `FILE_EXPORTS` machinery (registry currently empty, ingestion code intact) with code#1268 last-known retention.
- **Health model per source:** last-success timestamp, consecutive-failure count, failure **class** — `session-expired` / `cookie-missing` / `endpoint-changed` / `browser-down` / `cdp-unreachable` / `rate-limited` / `unknown` — each mapped to a repair.
- **Repair ladder, cheapest first,** attempt-capped and logged: (0) retain + disk-persisted cooldown (rate-limited only); (1) retry next tick; (2) re-validate/re-extract the session via CDP — primary pattern is the retired Meta producer's **in-page fetch, where the cookie never leaves the browser**; value extraction is the fallback and lands only in fleet secrets by name; (3) re-login in the browser via the standing Google SSO session ("click in and reset it") — a human-only challenge (2FA / verify-it's-you / passkey) makes the incident **human-blocked** and surfaces to Drew immediately; (4) escalate to a browser-enabled agent (fleet queue task with the full failure context + one deduplicated GitHub incident issue; auto-close on recovery).
- **State on disk, always:** `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-watchdog-state.json`, atomic writes. This is the direct application of code#5928's lesson — the watchdog is a oneshot and must not repeat the in-process cooldown/cache mistake.
- **Cadence:** producers `*:0/15`, watchdog offset on the same 15-min rhythm as the gatherer. **Alerting:** silent while self-repair works; Drew hears only human-blocked (immediately) or an escalation unresolved >24 h.
- **Generality:** per-provider **adapter** files (origins allowlist, data paths in preference order, cookie names, login hints, class map, thresholds). Mistral is adapter #1; Claude console / Open Design (code#5060) are named later adopters.
- **History:** health observations feed the existing usage snapshot pipeline (code#4889) once its laptop path bug is fixed; interim is the producers' `history.jsonl` convention — no parallel store.

## Position vs existing work

- This is the **quota-source specialization of code#1260** (pm-stack SLOs + self-healing: remediation catalogue, attempt caps/cooldowns, escalate only when remediation fails). Its catalogue entries fold back into #1260; code#1283 drills should eventually exercise it.
- It **revives the retired v1 Meta producer pattern** (CDP scrape, code#1301) for the one case the 2026-11-03 "quota is gathered by asking OpenCode" ruling does not cover: no API path exists at the credential class held. Preference order per source stays API → usage-capable token → browser-under-watchdog.
- Division of labor with openchamber#1619: that issue adds the Mistral key-validity provider (presence/validity via API). This program adds the **plan usage** read #1619 proved the API cannot give. Both land; neither replaces the other.

## Open questions (named, per #1260's rule)

1. Escalation-unresolved threshold before a NEEDS DREW line: 24 h proposed. Not blocking.
2. Recovery of a human-blocked incident: stay silent (closed issue is the record) — proposed.
3. Producer source home: `pm-stack/exporters/` in this repo (proposed) vs beside the quota module in openchamber.

## Implementation split (linked issues)

- Watchdog core: filed as a sibling issue in this repo, linked below.
- Escalation mechanism: filed as a sibling issue in this repo, linked below.
- Mistral adapter #1: filed in developing-today-forks/openchamber, **blocked on the sign-in lane's data-path outcome** (Vibe token usage API vs console endpoint + cookie), linked below.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] This design is reviewed and its open questions answered or explicitly deferred.
- [ ] The implementation issues linked from this issue exist and carry their own acceptance criteria (this issue carries no implementation work itself).
- [ ] The design's remediation-catalogue entries are reflected in code#1260's catalogue (comment or sub-issue link there).

items.body:
## Quota gatherer: every tick fails at import — lib dir resolves to a stale openchamber checkout parked on a queue branch

**Symptom (live 2026-11-04 evening):** `quota-gatherer.service` fails every tick in ~13ms with:

```
quota-gatherer: tick failed before providers ran: quota module import failed: auth.openCodeLocalCredentialSource is not a function. (In 'auth.openCodeLocalCredentialSource({ dbPath })', 'auth.openCodeLocalCredentialSource' is undefined)
```

(heartbeat `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-gatherer-heartbeat.json`, tickAt 2026-11-05T00:30:13Z, ok:false. Same failure at 18:18 and 18:23 CST ticks; the gatherer stall first observed 2026-11-04 ~18:30:15Z is consistent with this breakage starting earlier that day.)

**Root cause:** `resolveLibDir()` in `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/gather-quota.ts` picks the first candidate containing `quota/index.js`: `$OPENCHAMBER_LIB_DIR`, else `~/git/devtoday-openchamber/...` (doesn't exist), else `~/git/openchamber-fork/packages/web/server/lib`. The fork checkout `~/git/openchamber-fork` is currently parked on branch `queue/8357-224` (an old integration merge, e216864bf) with a dirty tree; its `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/auth.js` predates `openCodeLocalCredentialSource`. `origin/main` of the fork **has** the function (auth.js:214). The gatherer is therefore coupled to the mutable state of an unrelated work checkout — any queue lane that parks that checkout on an old branch breaks quota gathering fleet-wide, silently (heartbeat only).

**Verified workaround (used for the #5704 verification run):** a clean worktree of the fork at origin/main + `OPENCHAMBER_LIB_DIR=<worktree>/packages/web/server/lib` makes the gatherer run green.

**Fix options:**
1. Pin the deployed lib: set `OPENCHAMBER_LIB_DIR` in the quota-gatherer unit (Nix module) to a dedicated, main-tracking checkout/worktree of the fork that lanes never work in.
2. Vendor or bundle the quota module with the aggregator so no external checkout is on the runtime path.
3. At minimum: fail loud — a tick that dies at import should surface somewhere other than a heartbeat file (the stall went unnoticed for hours).

Do NOT fix by switching/cleaning `~/git/openchamber-fork` in place: it holds another lane's dirty queue work (queue/8357-224).

Found during the 2026-11-04 laptop-session coordinator run (Phase 2 of the #5704 verification — that fix itself is landed via PR #5719; the timer stays red until this issue is resolved).

Credential-scope smell, confirmed during the #5691 repoint (see TURSO-MIGRATION.md 2026-11-06 bullet-4 entry) and re-verified in the 2026-11-07 rename program (#6619).

~/tools/quota-check/JOB-BODY.md says the mirror reads use per-DB tokens by BWS name (turso.fleet-platform-rw-token / turso.fleet-mirror-rw-token, renamed 2026-11-07). In practice the reads go through `~/tools/bin/turso db shell <db>`, which authenticates with the turso CLI's PLATFORM token — one credential that can reach every database in the org. So:
- The per-DB tokens named in the job body are decorative on this route; rotating or revoking them does not change quota-check's access.
- A quota-check run holds org-wide DB authority when it only needs read access to two DBs (agent_quota_records on fleet-platform, agent_mirror_token_usage_daily on fleet-mirror).

Fix direction: make the quota-check reads use the per-DB tokens over the libsql HTTP pipeline (the pattern runtime-db-export's turso_client.py already implements, including its direct-BWS fallback for broker staleness #6767), or explicitly accept and document the platform-token route in the job body so the named tokens stop implying a scope they do not enforce.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] quota-check's mirror reads authenticate with the per-DB BWS tokens named in its job body (turso.fleet-platform-rw-token / turso.fleet-mirror-rw-token) over the libsql HTTP pipeline, OR the job body is explicitly corrected to document the platform-token route as accepted.
- [ ] If the per-DB route is adopted: revoking/rotating a per-DB token demonstrably changes quota-check's access to that DB only, and a quota-check run succeeds end-to-end on the new route.
- [ ] No quota-check run needs org-wide platform-token authority for its routine reads.

## Incident record — 2026-11-04 afternoon responsiveness loss (sandbox ↔ laptop path)

Drew's chat went unresponsive shortly after 15:00 CST ("connection error / reconnecting" at ~16:09, last activity ~15:0x). Two orchestration passes failed (14:12 no execution; 15:12 timeout after prelude). An independent workstream (Mistral-provider build, chat f3937a75) reported the fleet session proxy "closing EVERY CONNECT to the laptop (`laptop-agent: proxy closed during CONNECT` — three consecutive failures after earlier intermittent ones)". Drew powered the laptop OFF at ~17:01 CST and responsiveness returned — but the sandbox also recycled at 16:57 CST, which is the more mechanical explanation for the recovery (a fresh boot clears the wedged state, whatever it was).

### Timeline (UTC; CST = UTC−6)

- 14:38–20:57 — boots 0a18fb7e, da56f9ed (16:20), ad076b64 (18:27), d50de26a (20:57). Baseline load already high: resource sampler shows load 11–13 on 4 CPUs at 00:0x, and .rustdesk-wrapper ~45% CPU through the ad076b64 evening.
- ~20:43–21:16 — the repo-queue → fleet-queue migration completed (29 cron jobs) and the exceptions coordinator finished; heavy parallel agent work in flight (Atlas revision, Mistral build, ID sessions).
- 21:00–21:28 (boot d50de26a) — client trip log: **280 laptop-agent trips, ALL status 200**, 10–19/min, 15 slow (>5 s, worst 217 s — a long exec that completed). The laptop path itself was working. Load 2–8, mem avail 1.0–4.4 GB. Init re-running every 2–7 min in the background (see the init-loop issue — fixed separately).
- 21:22:46 — sandbox recycled again (boot 3ed35cc9, only 25 min after d50de26a).
- 21:25–21:29 — post-boot thundering herd: sampler shows load climbing; at **21:29:17 load 30.39 (1-min) / 12.61 (5-min), a `.gh-wrapped` process tree at 1645% CPU, and the Muse daemon restarted (pid 67 → 10918)**.
- **21:29:17 → 22:57 — the resource sampler produced NO further lines** (it had sampled every 2 min all day). Sandbox-side agent trips also essentially cease (2 trips in ~90 min vs ~280 in the prior 28 min). This ~88-minute window is Drew's dead period.
- 22:57:31 — sandbox recycled (boot 6989413c). Sampler, daemon, and trips resume immediately. Drew's connectivity returns ~17:01 CST (23:01 UTC) — in the new boot.
- After 23:01 — trips fail with ~25–32 s timeouts and `status: null` because the LAPTOP IS OFF (Drew powered it down) — expected, not a fault.

### What the evidence establishes

1. **The laptop and the laptop-agent path were not the failure** in the 21:00–21:28 window: 280/280 trips succeeded. The failure begins with a sandbox recycle (21:22) and a post-boot load explosion (21:29).
2. **The sandbox side wedged, not the transport**: a daemon restart + a sampler that stopped sampling for 88 minutes + agent traffic ceasing all point at the sandbox VM/daemon being frozen or CPU-starved, not at CONNECT refusals. (The Mistral agent's "proxy closed during CONNECT" errors are consistent with a sandbox-side proxy process starved/frozen mid-handshake — the broker log also holds a `ConnectionRefusedError` from `tunnel_socket` to the runtime proxy port and repeated client BrokenPipes — but the broker log has no timestamps, so those cannot be placed in the window. That is a logging gap to fix.)
3. **Recycle cadence is part of the story**: six boots on 2026-11-04 (02:25, 04:18, 06:03, 10:34, 12:33, 14:38, 16:20, 18:27, 20:57, 21:22, 22:57 — the sampler's boot list is even longer). Every recycle triggers catch-up cron firings + full init + the platform's apt replay; the 21:22 boot's herd is the one that tipped over.
4. **The fleet-queue migration is not implicated by any direct evidence**: migrated jobs invoke `fleet queue` on the sandbox, which reaches the queue-broker on the laptop through the same proxy pools as before; trip-log volume in the healthy window is agent execs (unchanged path), and no queue-connection errors appear in any timestamped log. The migration coincided with the incident window but the failure signature (daemon restart, sampler death) is sandbox CPU/life-cycle, not queue-client behavior. Remaining unknown: the Rust client's per-call connection behavior (pool reuse vs new CONNECT per call) — source is in the code repo (laptop, off at filing time); verify when it returns.
5. **Contributors, honestly weighted**: (a) post-boot thundering herd (catch-up crons + lanes + coordinators + platform apt replay) — strongest fit for the 21:29 spike; (b) the init re-run loop (fixed separately) added a ~65 s job every few minutes all day; (c) standing oversubscription — load 11–13 at idle-ish times on a 4-CPU box, .rustdesk-wrapper ~45% for hours; (d) a `.gh-wrapped` burst at 1645% at the spike moment (many agents shelling to gh simultaneously after the boot).

### What is NOT established (and the tests that settle it)

- **Concurrent-connection ceiling**: Drew's proposed clean ramp test (50 → 64 → 128 concurrent proxied connections sending real messages, find where errors start) has NOT been run — it needs the laptop ON (every proxied target terminates there). Run it when the laptop returns, against the queue-broker port and the daemon port, and record where "proxy closed during CONNECT" first appears, if anywhere.
- **Why the sampler stopped**: service death vs whole-VM freeze cannot be distinguished from surviving logs (the sampler's own log IS the missing data). sysstat collection (added 2026-11-04) would have answered this; ironically its install was blocked all day by the init-loop bug (now fixed), so the next incident should have sadc data.
- **Laptop-side state in the window** (broker/daemon logs, laptop load): pending — laptop is off by Drew's choice; gather when it returns: laptop trips.jsonl (daemon side), `fleet serve` broker journals, daemon journal for 21:00–22:10 UTC.
- **Why the platform recycled the sandbox at 21:22 and 22:57**: no platform-side reason is visible from inside the VM.

### Transport findings from the same pass (code-cited; full analysis in the investigation report)

- **"proxy closed during CONNECT" decoded**: the literal string (`laptop-agent.py:78`) fires on exactly one condition — EOF before the runtime proxy finishes answering a CONNECT. It is the **runtime proxy closing mid-handshake**, distinct from a refusal (non-200 → `CONNECT refused: …`) and from TCP-refused (an exception, surfaced via the broker as a 502). Three consecutive occurrences in the Mistral agent therefore mean the runtime proxy path itself was dropping handshakes during the window — consistent with the sandbox/runtime side being wedged, and NOT evidence of a laptop-daemon fault (the daemon is never reached when CONNECT itself fails).
- **Broker-mode failure chain**: in broker mode, that same EOF makes `tunnel_socket` raise `SystemExit`, which the Python broker's `except Exception` does not catch — the handler thread dies silently, the client sees "broker closed", auto-retries once, then falls back to a direct re-POST. A timed-out `/exec` can consequently be **submitted up to three times** (broker attempt + client retry + direct fallback). Duplicate-execution risk on long execs is a real, separate defect worth its own fix.
- **Broker ownership flaps between implementations**: the Python broker and `fleet proxy serve` share one socket; `broker.log` (untimestamped — a gap) shows them alternately owning it across boots, and at investigation time the **Python fallback was the live broker** — pool **12**, no overflow wait — while the fleet broker (pool **50**, 300 ms overflow wait) is what `init-ensure.sh` intends to launch with `LAPTOP_AGENT_POOL=50`. The two have materially different saturation behavior, so "which broker was live" is a variable in any future incident; making the broker log timestamped and the ownership deterministic belongs in the follow-ups.
- **The 660 s synchronous cap is ours**: `laptop-agent.py:108` (broker-socket timeout; the operative one) — a fleet-authored constant (daemon cap 600 + 60 headroom), not a platform default. The daemon caps a synchronous exec at **600 s total wall-clock per command** regardless of output (output is buffered, never streamed; there is no idle-timeout reset, and `/exec` has no stdin channel at all — interactive programs like vim cannot run over it; detached jobs are the multi-hour path).

### Actions taken in the same pass

- Init FAILURES=1 loop root-caused and fixed (separate issue): sysstat apt-lock deferral; the marker now gets written and init stops re-running per-prelude.
- Monitor + lane A + remaining `repo-queue` cron bodies migrated repo-first (hatch-personal a8f942c8d) per Drew's method.
- Trip-log v2 designed (separate issue): four timestamps per trip so the next incident attributes each leg.
- Quota-recorder laptop-broker redesign filed with recommendation (separate issue).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The incident timeline and root-cause analysis are complete on this issue.
- [ ] Every follow-up action is either filed as a linked issue or explicitly recorded as decided-against.
- [ ] The responsiveness-loss trigger (post-boot wedge) is named with the evidence that supports it.

## Why

On 2026-11-02 Drew ordered Supabase-only for the model/plan data: every Drive workbook was audited, the one gap was ingested, and the Drive files were renamed DEPRECATED (see the ainventory Maintenance_Log entry "Supabase-only consolidation", 2026-11-02). What remains is the table sprawl the workbook era left inside muse-dev2 itself: several overlapping stores hold the same facts, and reads keep landing in the wrong one. Concrete proof, same day: the AA Intelligence Index v5 load (2026-10-31) lives ONLY in `ainventory.sheet_rows` Rankings rows, while `measurement_events` and `benchmark_results` hold no v5 at all — a direct question about v5 data was first answered "we don't have it" because the event log was checked instead of the sheet mirror.

## Scope

**ainventory (first):**
- [ ] Decide the canonical store for benchmark facts. Three layers overlap today: `sheet_rows` (JSON-cell workbook mirror), `benchmark_results` (typed, workbook-era, frozen at the 2026-10-26 import), `measurement_events` (append-only event log, holds II v4.3.2 + CAI only). The 2026-10-26 design (#1248) names the event log as the target shape.
- [ ] Backfill the canonical store from Rankings AA|v5 + AA|v4.3.2 rows (incl. the 2026-11-02 source-44 rows: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 keying, cost/time fills) so no dataset exists only as sheet cells.
- [ ] Retire `benchmark_results` as a table — drop it or rebuild it as a view over the canonical store.
- [ ] Retire the deprecated alias view `v_latest_workbook_batch` (marked DEPRECATED 2026-11-02; use `v_latest_import_batch`). Consumers to migrate/audit first: the coding-plan-watch job (switched 2026-11-02), `ainventory_append.py`, the pm-aggregator AA collector/explorer (#3294, #3302 touch this surface).
- [ ] Data hygiene inside the sheet mirror: duplicate variant keys for the same model+effort (Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol each appear twice per effort — `|reasoning|` and `|yes|` key forms); the two `model_value_data` sources (ids 42 + 43) — keep both for provenance, dedupe at read time or via the canonical store.

**Other schemas:**
- [ ] automation / engineering / finance / home / research all carry the same workbook-era `sheet_rows` + `ingest_batches` + `sources` clone shape. Decide per domain: converge on the typed `events` shape their append helpers already write, or formally keep the mirror — no silent third state.
- [ ] `agent.mirror_*` tables: verify each mirror still has a live consumer; drop or document the ones nothing reads.

## Constraints

- No history loss: merges preserve provenance (source ids, import batches, snapshot dates, estimated-vs-measured flags such as the Rankings `|estimated` rows).
- No DROP before a consumer audit + readback verification of the replacement path (pm-aggregator collector, quota gatherer, coding-plan-watch, pool-intelligence all read this data).
- One schema/domain at a time, each step verified by readback before the next.
- Finish by updating `~/hatch-personal/workspace/supabase/ARCHITECTURE.md` so the documented shape matches reality.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Exactly one canonical read path per dataset, named in ARCHITECTURE.md.
- [ ] No live job, view, or doc references `v_latest_workbook_batch` or describes Drive workbooks as a data source.
- [ ] v5 benchmark data is queryable from the canonical store (not only from sheet cells).

Related: #1248 (the event-log design this executes), #3142 (pm stack into Supabase — adjacent, not this), #3294 / #3302 (AA explorer consumers).
